name: Jobab
overview: Jobab was a male Edomite who served as king of Edom, succeeding Bela in the royal lineage. His role as a ruler places him within the historical context of the Edomite tribes, highlighting his significance among the descendants of Esau. No additional personal details or notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jobab means 'howl' in Hebrew, as recorded in Genesis 36:33. This is the only name associated with him, and no further titles are noted beyond his kingship.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jobab was the son of Zerah, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jobab's significance lies in his position as a king of Edom, marking the continuation of Edomite leadership following Bela. His mention in the genealogical and royal records of Genesis emphasizes the structured succession of rulers among the Edomites, which contributes to the biblical understanding of the nations descending from Esau. Though brief, his record underscores God's providential oversight of historical lineages.
